headline: <mono>{count}</mono> references point to content from countries you haven't imported. That's normal.
tooltipContent:
A cross-country reference means one country's mod file references another country's entity (character / idea / focus, etc.).

HOI4 engine mod-loading rule: the engine loads all mod files together, and any country's event can fire for any country, as long as its trigger is met.

In the editor: references are filtered by the active country, and viewing them doesn't switch your primary country. Adding a secondary country pulls the related entities in without affecting your primary view.

Example: britain.1 (the Tizard mission) in Britain.txt has trigger tag = USA. The event's "owner" is USA, but the file lives in Britain.txt and its namespace is britain, so the cross-ref banner suggests adding USA or ENG as a secondary country to pull the entity in.
reason: These almost always reference other countries' content, and they're harmless. A “merge back into the original mod” (Path B) export keeps them intact, so nothing is lost. Want that content in the editor too? Add a country below. Your primary country won't change.
suggestLabel: Suggested countries to add (by reference count):
expandTitle: Adding {tag} as a secondary country expands the project's country list. It doesn't switch your primary country; the primary view stays unchanged.
scopeNote: Reference types not yet covered (focus / decision / trait / tech, etc.) will be added in later batches. "Not reported" doesn't mean "no problem".

unmodeled.headline: Found <mono>{count}</mono> references to content the program doesn't model
unmodeled.tooltipContent:
The program models 9 entity types (idea / event / focus / decision / character / trait / technology / opinion modifier / MIO). Other HOI4 categories — scripted effects/triggers, ideologies, cosmetic tags, game rules, equipment, special projects — aren't modeled, so the program can't re-emit their definition files.

References to them are valid HOI4 script. A "merge back into the original mod" (Path B) export keeps the original definition files, so the references resolve. A from-scratch (Path A) export can't reproduce them, so they would dangle.

This is informational, not an error — the program just wants you to know which export path keeps these intact.
unmodeled.note: These references point at content the program doesn't model yet (e.g. custom scripted_effect / scripted_trigger, custom ideologies, cosmetic tags). They are kept only by the “merge back into the original mod” (Path B) export; a from-scratch (Path A) export leaves them dangling. If you export via Path B, no action is needed.
